title: Linear time bounds from simulation relations
statement: Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme, let $U$ be a finite-tape binary machine, and let $S,B$ be functions assigning natural-number bounds to bit strings. Suppose a relation is specified between configurations of the machine decoded from each $\alpha$ on input $x$ and configurations of $U$ on the paired encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$. Assume that for every $\alpha,x$, a related pair is reached from the two initial configurations after some number of steps; each related pair advances to a related pair when the source takes one step and $U$ takes between $1$ and $B(\alpha)$ steps; related configurations halt simultaneously; and related configurations have equal outputs. Then for every $\alpha$ there is a natural number $C$ such that, for every $x$, any output computed by the decoded machine within $t$ steps is computed by $U$ within $C(t+1)$ steps, and every output computed by $U$ at some time is computed by the decoded machine at some time.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ assigns a natural-number bound to each bit string
$B$ assigns a natural-number bound to each bit string
A relation is given for every code string and input between source and target configurations
For every $\alpha,x$, some related pair is reached from the two initial configurations within $S(\alpha)$ target steps
For every related pair, the source one-step successor is related to a target configuration reached in $d$ steps with $1\le d\le B(\alpha)$
For every $\alpha$ there is a natural number $C$ satisfying both computation implications
replaced:
Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme, let $U$ be a finite-tape binary machine,
and let $S,B$ assign natural-number bounds to each bit string. Suppose a relation is
given, for every code string $\alpha$ and input $x$, between configurations of the
machine decoded from $\alpha$ on $x$ and configurations of $U$ on
$\langle\alpha,x\rangle$. Assume that for every $\alpha,x$, a related pair is reached
from the two initial configurations within $S(\alpha)$ steps of $U$; that each related
pair advances from the source machine’s one-step successor to a related target
configuration in between $1$ and $B(\alpha)$ target steps; that related configurations
halt simultaneously; and that related configurations have equal outputs. Then for every
$\alpha$ there is a constant $C$ such that, for every input $x$, any output computed by
the decoded machine within $t$ steps is computed by $U$ on $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$
within $C(t+1)$ steps, and every output computed by $U$ on that paired input at some
time is computed by the decoded machine on $x$ at some time.
